questions.question: Transmission electron microscope uses______ for imaging.
The true sample thickness of TEM sample can be measured using______.
Which technique requires the sample to be thinned to less than 100 nm?
Why is TEM preferred over SEM for imaging nanoscale precipitates?

answers.a: TEM provides higher resolution due to electron transmission through the sample.
answers.b: SEM has a higher resolution than TEM.
answers.d: SEM uses transmitted electrons, making it more suitable for nanoscale imaging.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major advantage of TEM over SEM for analysing precipitate morphology?

answers.a: TEM provides diffraction contrast, helping in phase identification.
answers.b: SEM can easily image atomic structures.
answers.c: TEM has a lower resolution than SEM.
answers.d: TEM can only be used for surface imaging.

questions.question: What is the primary limitation of SEM when imaging nanoscale precipitates?

answers.a: SEM uses lower-energy electrons, reducing resolution.
answers.b: SEM requires ultra-thin samples for imaging.
answers.c: SEM detects secondary and backscattered electrons, which have limited spatial resolution.
answers.d: SEM cannot operate at high magnifications.
